whyWatch.body:
Both Tubi matches are group stage openers for host nations, which means opening week carries a little extra weight.

Mexico plays in Mexico City on June 11. The US plays in Los Angeles on June 12. Home advantage is real, but so is the pressure that comes with it. Paraguay and South Africa are not here to make anyone look good, and neither crowd is going to get an easy afternoon.

Create your free Tubi account before the tournament starts. Registration takes about a minute, and it keeps the live match experience clean when kickoff arrives. If you miss the live window, the replay is up within 1 to 2 hours and does not require an account.

items.heading: Mexico vs. South Africa, June 11, 1:00 PM CT
items.paragraph: Mexico opens Group A at Mexico City Stadium in front of a home crowd that will give the tournament its first big roar. South Africa arrives with something to prove, which is exactly the kind of tension that makes a group stage opener worth watching. Fox Pregame runs before kickoff, and the match streams live on Tubi with a free account.

items.heading: USA vs. Paraguay, June 12, 6:00 PM PT
items.paragraph: The USMNT plays its first World Cup match on home soil since 1994 at Los Angeles Stadium in Inglewood. Paraguay brings a real test into Group D, where Australia and Türkiye are also waiting. Weston McKennie, Ricardo Pepi, and Sergiño Dest lead the US side into a match that will feel personal for anyone who has been waiting to see this tournament back on American soil.

items.heading: Fox Pregame, both match days
items.paragraph: Both match days open with Fox Pregame before kickoff. You get team news, lineup context, and the stadium atmosphere building in real time. For opening matches especially, that buildup matters. The pressure, the nerves, and the first big storylines of the tournament start showing up before the ball ever moves.
